steps: Blend all ingredients in a blender until smooth.
Add water if a more liquid consistency is desired.
Add the frozen bananas, frozen berries and oat milk to a blender.
Blend on high until thick and smooth, stopping to scrape down the sides if the mixture is too stiff to move.
Pour into a bowl - it should be thick enough to hold its shape like soft-serve.
Scatter over the hemp seeds and granola.
Top with the sliced fruit and eat immediately.
Run the frozen açaí packs under warm water for a few seconds, then bash the packs to break the açaí into chunks.
Blend the açaí chunks with one banana and the guaraná syrup or honey, adding only a splash of liquid if needed, until thick and smooth.
Pour into a bowl - the mixture should be thick enough to hold a spoon upright.
Slice the second banana and arrange it over the top with the granola.
Serve straight away before it melts.
Toast the bread slices until golden and crisp.
Halve the avocado, remove the stone and scoop the flesh into a bowl.
Mash the avocado roughly with a squeeze of lime juice and a pinch of sea salt.
Spread the mashed avocado over the toast.
Scatter with chilli flakes, drizzle with olive oil and finish with an extra squeeze of lime.
Toast the bread slices until golden.
Tip the chickpeas into a bowl and mash with a fork until mostly smooth with some texture left.
Mash the avocado into the chickpeas with a squeeze of lemon juice, the olive oil and a pinch of salt.
Spread the mixture over the toast.
Finish with a scatter of chilli flakes and an extra squeeze of lemon.
Divide the Greek yogurt evenly between 5 jars or containers.
Spoon the granola over each in an even layer.
Top each jar with the mixed berries.
Drizzle each jar with a little honey.
Seal and refrigerate until ready to grab and go.
Spoon the coconut yogurt into a bowl.
Stir the chia seeds through the yogurt.
Dice the mango and scatter it over the top with the granola.
Finish with a drizzle of maple syrup.
Rinse the amaranth in a sieve, then tip it into a small pan with the water.
Bring to the boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook for 18-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and creamy.
Remove from the heat and stir in the chia seeds, letting the porridge sit for a minute to thicken further.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the mixed berries, hemp seeds and pumpkin seeds.
Drizzle with maple syrup and serve warm.
Position a rack in the center of the oven and preheat to 350 degrees.
Line a 12-cup standard muffin tin with paper muffin cups.
In a large bowl, combine the almond meal, oats, cinnamon and walnuts or currants.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the eggs, zucchini, carrot, melted butter and maple syrup.
Add to the dry ingredients, mixing until just combined.
Spoon the batter into the muffin cups, filling each to the brim.
Bake until the muffins are nicely browned on top and a knife inserted in the center of a muffin comes out clean, 25 to 30 minutes.
Allow muffins to cool completely before storing.
Whisk the chia seeds into the coconut or oat milk with the maple syrup and a drop of vanilla.
Let the mixture sit for 5 minutes, then whisk again to break up any clumps.
Divide between 3 jars or containers, cover and refrigerate overnight until thickened to a pudding consistency.
Dice the mango and stir or layer it through each pudding before serving.
In a small pot, bring the stock to a boil over medium heat.
Add the oats and simmer for 10 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the oats are close to your desired consistency.
Add salt, pepper and everything-bagel seasoning in the final few minutes of cooking.
While the oats finish, fry the egg in the olive oil and slice the avocado.
Spoon the oats into a bowl, top with the fried egg and avocado, and eat immediately.
Finish with a dash of hot sauce.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat and slice the mushrooms.
Fry the mushrooms for 3-4 minutes until softened and browned, then add the spinach and cook until just wilted.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and pour over the mushrooms and spinach in the pan.
Cook for 2-3 minutes, gently drawing the edges into the centre, until the base is set.
Fold the omelette in half once the top is just set, then slide onto a plate.
Serve with the orange juice on the side.
Heat the olive oil in a large pan and fry the diced onion and red pepper for 5-6 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic, cumin and paprika and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the tinned tomatoes, season, and simmer for 15-18 minutes until thickened into a rich sauce.
Make small wells in the sauce, crack in the eggs, then cover and cook for 5-6 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still soft.
Crumble the feta over the top and serve straight from the pan with the crusty bread.
Preheat the oven to 180°C and grease or line a 12-hole muffin tin.
Whisk the eggs in a large jug with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Divide the cooked crumbled sausage and spinach evenly between the muffin holes.
Pour the whisked egg over each, filling to just below the rim.
Bake for 18-20 minutes until puffed and set in the centre.
Cool for a few minutes before turning out; store in the fridge for up to 4 days.
